   COE supply for 3-month period until Jan 2027 to go up by 1.1%
 Sign up now: Get ST's newsletters delivered to your inbox
 The supply of COEs for smaller and less powerful cars and EVs remains unchanged from the current three-month quota period.
 ST PHOTO: LIM YAOHUI
 Lee Nian Tjoe
 Published   Oct 26, 2026, 06:20 PM
 Updated   Oct 26, 2026, 10:00 PM
 Set as preferred source Listen SINGAPORE – The number of certificates of entitlement (COEs) available for bidding for the three-month period from November 2026 to January 2027 will increase by 1.1% to 19,298.
 That works out to an increase of 213 certificates from the 19,085 certificates in the current August to October period.
 The Land Transport Authority (LTA), in a statement on Oct 26, said the number of Category B COEs for the November to January period will go up to 5,707.
 That is a 3.3% increase from the 5,527 certificates made available for the current three-month period.
 This translates into 30 more COEs at each of the coming six tender exercises compared with the current period.
 That means the increase in the number of COEs for the next batch is somewhat smaller than it was for the previous three-month period, in which Category B supply rose by 6.2%, or 322 more certificates.
 COEs give people the right to own a vehicle in Singapore, and Category B certificates are meant for larger and more powerful cars and electric vehicles (EVs). There are two tender exercises held each month.
 The number for Category A certificates – for smaller and less powerful cars and EVs – remains unchanged at 7,134. This is the first time Category A supply did not dip after three straight quarters of reductions.
 Category C COE supply, for commercial vehicles and buses, will go up by 2% from 1,836 to 1,873.
 Open category COEs or Category E supply will increase 3.7% to 1,580, from 1,523 certificates. This category of COEs can be used to register any vehicle type other than motorcycles but tend to be used for larger, costlier cars.
 Being transferrable, motor dealers often secure them for the flexibility to register cars without waiting for the next tender exercise.
 Motorcycle COEs (Category D) is the only COE category to post a dip in supply. At 3,004 certificates, the supply for the upcoming quota period is 2% lower than the 3,065 certificates for the August to October period.
 The number of certificates available for bidding is mainly driven by the rolling average of deregistrations in the previous four quarters.
 Contributing to the COE supply are certificates that have been identified as certainly expiring in the peak supply period, and which are brought forward for redistribution.
 The redistributed certificates in COE supply for the next three months include 61 certificates for commercial vehicles and 1,031 for motorcycles but none for categories A and B.
 The supply bump comes amid a recent trend of soaring COE premiums linked to strong buying demand.
 At the most recent tender exercise on Oct 21 , Category A COEs hit $132,004 while Category B cost $131,901.
 It marked the fourth time in 2026 that COEs for smaller and less powerful cars and EVs were pricier than certificates for larger and more powerful cars and EVs.
 An ongoing public consultation exercise to review the COE categorisation framework will close on Nov 2, 11.59pm. People can go to https://go.gov.sg/coe-pcd-feedback to provide feedback.

 Ron Lim, sales and marketing head of Tan Chong Motor Sales, said the upcoming supply of COEs across all categories is “within expectations”. He added that the number of Category A certificates available has already peaked while the supply of Category B COEs will continue to grow.
 Lim said he expects Category A premiums to stay high, and maybe even overtake Category B prices. He added that the trend will not change unless the COE framework is changed.
 Premium Automobiles managing director Lee Hoe Lone said there is an ongoing rush to register cars in 2026, ahead of a cut in incentives for EVs, and higher penalties for non-electric cars. That is likely to keep COE prices high, he added.
 Premium Automobiles distributes Chinese EV brands like Avatr, Changan and Zeekr.
 Uncertainty about how COE rules will change after the review and pressure to hit year-end sales targets could push demand past the number of COEs available, said Raymond Ng, managing director of Eurokars EV, which distributes the Chinese brands MG and IM Motors.
 When asked what could happen after EV incentives are reduced, Ng said it is unclear how the COE framework will be changed, so the “crystal ball is still a bit cloudy for now”.
 Lee Nian Tjoe is senior transport correspondent at The Straits Times, where he also oversees the Motoring section.
